messages:
sara: Heads-up — found an authz bug in GraphQL presignedUpload. presigned URL returned even when caller lacks access to the target org. Repro in staging.

sara: Repro steps (staging):
```graphql
mutation {
  presignedUpload(input:{orgId:"org_abc", filename:"test.png", size:12345}) {
    url
    key
  }
}
```

alex: Ack. Do we have logs for who called it and when? @devsec-bot any alerts? :eyes:

devsec-bot: Alert created: presign_authz_failure_detected (high). LogID: log-20240322-09-2334

tim: I pulled the app logs. Sample: `INFO presign request userId=u_9832 orgId=org_abc result=OK presigner=uploads-service` — weird, result shows OK even though permission check downstream should have rejected.

sara: Exactly. Looks like the permission check on the mutation handler runs after we call the presigner service. So service will give a valid presigned url before we enforce RBAC.

jordan: Containment: 1) Flip feature flag to disable public presigns for org-scoped uploads in staging/prod. 2) Add temporary WAF rule to block requests with mutation name `presignedUpload` from unauthenticated clients. 3) Revoke any elevated deploy keys? Note: presigned urls themselves can't be revoked; we need to rotate the S3 upload token or change object prefixes.

maria: For prod rollout we should rotate the KMS key used to sign policy if presign generation depends on it, and kick an S3 policy change so existing presigned urls expire earlier (shorten TTL). Also add an audit event on presign generation that includes evaluated principal and parent resource id.

sara: Proposed immediate patch (hotfix): move authz check to run before presigner call and fail fast. Minimal diff:
```diff
- const presign = await presigner.create(...)
- if (!canAccess(user, org)) throw Forbidden
+ if (!canAccess(user, org)) throw Forbidden
+ const presign = await presigner.create(...)
```

alex: Good. Also add a unit test asserting presign not returned for user without org membership. Add an integration check in staging that attempts exploit path every deploy.

tim: I'll open a short-lived sprint ticket and tag eng-oncall to push the hotfix. Oncall: can you schedule a canary deploy to staging, then prod if green?

eng-oncall: On it. Pushing hotfix to staging now, will run automated exploit test and smoke tests. ETA ~25m.

maria: Post-incident follow-ups: 1) Audit logs: ensure presign events stored in centralized audit stream with retention. 2) RBAC: add server-side guard that enforces resource-based checks before any external call. 3) KMS rotation checklist. 4) Postmortem doc + customer comms draft if we confirm any external exposure.

sara: Agreed. For customer comms we need severity assessment — right now only staging confirmed. If prod exploit tests are negative we still run rotation and extended logging.

jordan: I'm adding a temporary metric on presign generation failures/success to alert on anomalous rates. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sara: Thanks all — will update this thread after staging canary results. :white_check_mark:
